A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TS-Reasoner and retain matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original TimeSeriesExam and MTBench evaluations, scaling experiments, component ablations, and quantitative caption-diversity analysis.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds open-ended reasoning evaluation, further controlled comparisons, evaluator validation, and contamination analysis.

M1.justification: V1 Section 3.1 specifies zero-mean/unit-variance normalization; v2 Section 3.3 specifies mean centering, conditional rescaling, and textual offset/scale tokens. This revises the stated input procedure while retaining the architecture and two-stage training. However, v2 Appendix A retains the old normalization description, leaving the implemented procedure unclear.

E1.justification: V2 adds the Inductive Reasoning dataset, requiring open-ended explanations of physical principles from univariate or multivariate series (Section 4.7). This substantially extends evaluation beyond the retained multiple-choice TimeSeriesExam and MTBench tasks. Training-data sources remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds DeepSeek-R1 to the existing benchmark comparison while retaining the earlier comparators. The new open-ended comparison also introduces GPT-4o-mini in textual and visual modes and Qwen2.5-14B. Appendix C's architectural comparison does not establish additional experimental baselines.

E3.justification: V2 introduces RAGAS keyword-based scoring for open-ended answers and a 100-case manual validation procedure. It also adds a same-training-pipeline textual-input control and revises stated preprocessing and embedding dimensions. Existing training budgets remain unchanged; the revised descriptions do not establish that all earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative textual-versus-visual captioning comparisons, a Chronos encoder variant, '-Freeze' and TS-as-text ablations, input-length and modality-reliance analyses, a template-versus-generated caption case study, and contamination checks. The earlier lexical-diversity study and three-way captioning case study are retained, with the former moved into the main text.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without documented uncertainty estimation. V2 Table 2 adds TS-Reasoner means and standard deviations across three inference runs of one checkpoint using different seeds. Tables 2 and 6 add McNemar significance tests at p<0.05. These quantify inference variability, not variability across independently trained models.

E6.justification: Reported TimeSeriesExam overall accuracy changes from 54.26 to 54.83±0.98, and finance-long accuracy from 90.12 to 92.00±1.74. These updated estimates use newly specified inference averaging and do not establish same-protocol gains. Added results include 54.70 on open-ended reasoning, 49.67 TimeSeriesExam accuracy for TS-as-text, and 0% detected 13-gram contamination on the original benchmarks.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.1 newly defines the output as a reasoning path followed by an answer, V=[R;A], and factorizes its conditional probability in Equation 1. This is a limited formal addition; the existing embedding equations are retained, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the abstract's performance claim to open-source models of comparable scale and similarly qualifies the introduction. The central contributions—frozen-TSFM alignment, attribute-aware captioning, two-stage training, and data efficiency—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving backbone reasoning capacity, smaller-model limitations, greater TSFM benefit for longer inputs, and compensation from textual context. It adds privacy/cost deployment discussion and treats MTBench as supplementary. V1's explicit resource-constrained 7B limitation paragraph is removed, although v2 discusses capacity-related performance boundaries elsewhere.

D1.justification: V2 adds code, model-weight and training-data links, a single-layer GELU adapter specification, approximately 20/5-hour stage timings, and benchmark prompts in Figures 13–15. It revises the stated LLM/TSFM embedding dimensions from 5120/1080 to 3584/1280. Existing training hyperparameters and hardware information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands comparative positioning through Appendix C and Table 8, contrasting ChronoSteer, TempoGPT and Time-VLM by transfer direction, representation, training data, frozen components and evaluation tasks. It also adds citations including CoRA, TSRouter, TSRBench, RAGAS and contamination-analysis precedents, while retaining the central pretrained-TSFM positioning.

P1.justification: V2 reorganizes the method into formulation, overview, architecture and training subsections. Implementation details move from Appendix A into Section 4, and caption-diversity analysis moves from Appendix C into Section 4.6. Results explanations are rewritten and condensed, and the appendix structure is extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different journal layout, enlarges and relocates figures, and restyles Figure 6 with truncated vertical axes. Tables gain uncertainty and significance formatting. New displays include the caption-representation comparison, another caption case study, benchmark prompts, and open-ended, architectural-comparison, input-length and contamination tables.

improvement.justification: V1's reasoning evidence relied on multiple-choice evaluations without reported uncertainty. V2 substantially strengthens validation through human-checked open-ended evaluation, a matched-training textual-input control, statistical reporting and contamination analysis, while improving reproducibility documentation and narrowing headline claims. The conflicting normalization descriptions and inference-only uncertainty remain limitations, but the added evidence addresses important weaknesses in the earlier paper.
